references.text: Moses describes the promised land with cities they did not build, houses full of good things they did not fill, wells they did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees they did not plant - this is the same theme as in Joshua 24:13.
Description of the good land the Lord gives Israel, with water, wheat, barley, vines, figs, pomegranates, olive oil, and honey - God's gift of a fertile land they did not have to work to create.
The spies report on the land's fertility with grapes, pomegranates, and figs - evidence of the fruitful land God promised to give them.
The psalm praises God for giving Israel the lands of the nations, so that they took possession of others' labor - a direct reference to the same event described in Joshua 24:13.

Nehemiah describes how the fathers took fortified cities and fertile land, houses full of good things, wells, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance - a direct parallel to Joshua 24:13.
Isaiah sings about the Lord's vineyard which He planted and tended - in contrast to the vineyards Israel received without their own labor in Joshua 24:13.
The warning that others will harvest what they plant - the opposite situation of the blessing in Joshua 24:13 where Israel harvested what others had planted.
